status_meanings.PROPOSED: Written at implementation grade. No evidence yet. Default.

notes.verification_2026_09_09: Task 1 verification against origin/main f13219b. Every non-PROPOSED status was checked against the repository; entries carry `verified` and, where a repository claim exists, `evidence`. Nothing was downgraded: every error found ran in the direction of UNDERSTATING what exists, so no aspirational claim needed removing. Four corrections of substance: (1) factory_kernel/state.py no longer exists - audit finding B.4 was closed by PR #43, which DELETED the unexecuted state machine, and a regression test now forbids its return; (2) the holdout is genuinely builder-blind via sparse checkout since PR #42, so B.3 is closed; (3) per-stage timing instrumentation is substantially present (record_stage_timing / stage-timings.jsonl), not absent; (4) the merge verifier does enforce byte-identical tree equivalence. Two facts the corpus has no entry for: the measured floors now lag observed evidence by a wide margin (floor unit_tests=1033 and static_checks=5 against an observed UNIT_PASSED tests=2353 and STATIC_OK checks=6 on the same quick gate, run 34332642132), and the daily full-harness regression on main has failed every day since 2026-09-05 at GATE_FAILED: e2e (issue #119).

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: never attribute a refusal to an authority that did not produce it
decisions.rationale: The Honesty invariant forbids displaying passed/verified unless the real authority produced that result. Its mirror is missing, and the asymmetry has a measured cost. runtime.py sets stage='merge_preauth' before the merge_verify.py pre call and never advances it; merge_squash is invoked ~20 lines later with the cursor unchanged. The failure was a RuntimeError from run_as_app, not a ToolRefused, so refusal.classify() skipped the isinstance branch - including the correct discriminator sitting in it (exc.tool == 'merge_verify.py' and exc.phase == 'pre') - and fell through to `if stage in STAGE_CODES: return stage`. The system named an authority that had already recorded outcome=ok in the same run. This mis-attributes ANY non-ToolRefused exception raised after the last cursor assignment in a stage sequence: structural, not a one-off. Four minutes of diagnosis became four days; issue #119 collected four repeat reports while the 401 sat in the logs. Every guarantee in this system points at proving success honestly and nothing points at reporting failure honestly. MEASURED COST, the strongest argument this amendment has: four days of diagnosis, and then two more with the PR parked. The artifacts said retry the merge -- merge-authorization.json written, the spine closed, merge-pre outcome=ok -- so the correct action was one command. The label said merge pre-authorization refused it, which reads as evidence work. Six days and four repeat reports on issue #119, from one wrong word in a refusal that was itself correct. A wrong diagnosis is not a smaller defect than a wrong verdict; it is the same defect pointed at whoever reads it next.
decisions.cost: an hour, plus the constitutional paragraph
decisions.note: Asks for three things. (1) The invariant stated in 01-CONSTITUTION.md beside Honesty. (2) classify() must not name an authority on the fallthrough path: unattributed failures report the stage as CONTEXT, not attribution - `stage=merge_preauth authority=unattributed`. (3) An adversarial test that injects a non-ToolRefused exception after a passing authority and asserts the refusal does not name it. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: an earlier draft proposed validating attribution against the stage-timings artifact. Rejected - timings are observability only ('nothing reads this file to decide anything'), and making the classifier depend on them would turn an observational artifact into a semi-trusted input, which is DFC-072 (references are not authority) in a new place. Not naming an authority on the fallthrough path is structural rather than heuristic, and is the whole fix. OBSERVABLE SIGNATURE, confirmed live in run 34371899263: the refusal record carries both `stage` and `stage_context`, and they AGREE exactly when the cursor is open and DIVERGE when it is closed (`stage` empty, `stage_context` naming the last authority entered). That gives the invariant a field test, not just a suite test: any refusal whose two fields agree was attributed by an authority that was still executing, and any refusal naming an authority with an empty `stage` is the defect returning. The stale_base refusal at 0.622 s into trust_root_currency read stage=trust_root_currency stage_context=trust_root_currency reason_code=stale_base -- the half that must keep working, proven before the expensive half was run.

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: split the unit floor three ways - factory, backend, frontend
decisions.rationale: 1798 of the 2353 tests the unit rung counts are the factory's own trust-root suite. Welded into one number, a product PR is gated on a count dominated by maintainer hardening; conversely product tests can be deleted while the total still rises. Trust-root tests grow when the factory is hardened, product tests when features ship. They ratchet on different clocks and belong in different keys.
decisions.cost: half a day across three files
decisions.note: floor.json gains unit_tests_factory / unit_tests_backend / unit_tests_frontend; unit_tests is retired or kept transitionally as the sum. Three coordinated edits: harness/ci.py must stop discarding unit.py's stdout on success (unit.py has emitted `backend= frontend= factory=` all along and nothing has ever seen it); scripts/factory_evidence.py must parse the three fields - the `semantic_markers` block there already shows how to make a floor key optional ('when present here'), so this lands additively with no flag day; floor.json gains the keys. SETTLES A LIVE CONTRADICTION in the same change: unit.py's docstring still says the ratchet is 'based on the last measured backend+frontend total ... factory tests are mandatory immediately without inventing a higher floor'. True at 549; falsified when the 2026-09-04 note moved the floor to the all-three total without touching it. SEQUENCING: do not ratchet to 1798/430/125. Those are inferred from arithmetic (they reproduce both 1033 at d038e93 and 2353 at f13219b exactly) but no run has ever printed them. Land the ci.py change, take the observed values from the next green gate, then ratchet with zero slack, per floor.json's own _raise_these rule.

decisions.cost: one line

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: a PR that changes the number of checks or tests must touch floor.json
decisions.rationale: Three instances of one defect in three weeks: floor 549 against an observed 766 (audit finding B.5, diagnosed and corrected); unit_tests 1033 against an observed 2353; static_checks 5 against an observed 6. Three is a pattern, not three accidents. DFE-015 and DFE-016 are each symptomatic of it. The ratchet mechanism is assumed to be self-enforcing and demonstrably is not: it depends on a human remembering, on the same change, and the memory has failed every time it was tested. BEARS DIRECTLY ON DFE-012: ACP-003's argument assumes the ratchet family works as a mechanism. Adding a fourth dial to a mechanism that is not being turned is the wrong order. This lands first.
decisions.cost: a deterministic check plus its mutation
decisions.note: Shape: a check that refuses a PR which changes the count a floor measures without changing floor.json. Cheap for static (the CHECKS list is enumerable statically); for unit it needs the observed count, so the honest form is probably a comparison of observed against floor with a required acknowledgement in the diff rather than a purely static test. Belongs in the security guard's ratchet_regressions neighbourhood, which already asserts floor(head) >= floor(base) on both lanes - the missing half is that a floor may not stay still while what it measures moves.

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: the autonomous identity is minted per operation, not once per job
decisions.rationale: The App installation token is minted once per job and read per operation. Tokens live 60 minutes; the three operations that spend the identity span up to 95 minutes and the exact-head merge is by construction the latest. No autonomous PR can merge, because the credential authorising the merge expires before the validation that earns it finishes. Measured: create_pr for PR #134 fired at +56m27s (3m33s of credential life left); merge_squash fired at +94m38s and returned 401 Bad credentials, after the evidence stage (4970.989s) and merge-pre both recorded outcome=ok. A credential-lifetime defect that surfaced at the last spend point, not a merge defect - fixing only the merge leaves a live fault two spend points upstream.
decisions.cost: bounded; a workflow step split plus a refusal code
decisions.note: See 12-ACP-004-AUTONOMOUS-IDENTITY-LIFETIME.md. Tier 2 because it lands in the credential broker, NOT because the design is in question: re-minting costs nothing and weakens nothing, and the capability stays narrow, scoped, one-shot and fallback-free. Rejects giving the kernel the App private key (TCB widening to fix a clock). The exact-head guarantee survives a step split because merge_verify.py pre already writes merge-authorization.json binding base/head/tree/evidence hash and the post check re-verifies against the actual merge commit. Refusal margin 20 minutes, set against observed spend-point ages rather than the 60-minute limit - a five-minute margin would have permitted the 56m27s spend that nearly failed. Falsifier: a build whose validation exceeds TWO HOURS merges successfully with every spend point verifiably younger than its own mint. Makes no claim that wall time is a correctness constraint; that is true only while the credential is misused.

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: split the build's push/PR handoff behind its own mint
decisions.rationale: ACP-004 protected the spend with 95 minutes of headroom and left unprotected the one that came within 3m33s. On run 34061371205 the build called push_branch and create_pr at +56m27s against a 3600s token. merge_squash now runs behind its own mint; push_branch and create_pr still run at the end of one long dispatch step, on the identity minted before it. THE CURRENT FAILURE MODE IS A PUSHED BRANCH WITH NO PR: push_branch spends the identity first, so a build that crosses the hour between the two calls leaves a branch on the remote that no pull request references, and the run that could have finished it is gone. That is worse than the merge failure it mirrors, because the merge at least refused with the evidence intact.
decisions.cost: a design question, then a workflow step
decisions.note: Why it was not done inside ACP-004: item 1 was cheap because merge-authorization.json already existed, so the merge step's entire input was on disk and the split cost a CLI entry point. The build handoff has no equivalent artifact - it carries worktree, env, paths, attempt, branch and issue in memory - and inventing one is the actual work. THE OPEN QUESTION IS THE OVERLAP WITH RESUME: `resume_pr` (D-033/D-034) already finishes a build from its uploaded artifacts, but at a LATER seam, after the PR exists. This needs the seam one step earlier, before push_branch. Either the handoff artifact is designed so resume becomes a special case of it, or there are two near-identical recovery paths and the second one will drift from the first. Decide that before writing either. Until this lands, github_cli.SPLIT_OPERATIONS holds only merge_squash and the two unsplit operations print FACTORY_IDENTITY_AGE and proceed rather than refusing - refusing at 1200s what currently succeeds at 3387s would be a regression dressed as a fix. Those age lines are the evidence that will size this work. SCOPE NARROWED by run 34374035444: this is a BUILD-PATH exposure, not a general unsplit-spend exposure. The re-head's push_branch spent an identity 451 s old, comfortably inside the 1200 s margin, because the re-head is a short path -- red gate, green gate, conformance, final green, quick gate, then push. The build is long because it runs nine model stages before its handoff, which is why create_pr fired at 3387 s there. So the work is to split the BUILD's handoff; the re-head's push is already safe by construction and needs no artifact, no new seam and no resume overlap. That halves the design question: only build_issue needs a handoff artifact, and rehead_pr can be left alone.

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: only stale_base has a model-free recovery path; every other refusal is terminal
decisions.rationale: rehead_eligible requires the latest refusal to be stale_base, so a PR refused for any other reason is skipped by the dispatcher and refused by `rehead` when run by hand. PR #134 passed the entire ladder on 2026-09-07, was refused at the merge by an expired credential, and has been inert since: not eligible for validation (needs-fix, not needs-review) and not eligible for re-head (reason code merge_preauth, not stale_base). Neither DFE-014 nor DFE-018 changes that -- they would have classified the same failure `unknown` and `identity_expired`, and neither is stale_base either. The gap is in the recovery model, not the classifier: a refusal whose cause is infrastructure rather than evidence has no automatic path back, and a human must drive it.
decisions.cost: a design question: which reason codes admit a model-free repair, and what each repair is
decisions.note: Filed 2026-09-09 while hand-driving #134 back into the queue -- a PR the factory could have recovered itself had the reason code been different. The demonstration is the evidence. Not to be folded into DFE-014 or DFE-018: both are about naming a failure correctly, this is about what the system may do once it has. Candidate shape: identity_expired admits a model-free retry (the evidence is intact and bound; only the credential was stale), which is a strictly smaller repair than a re-head. Do not generalise past the codes whose repair can be shown to preserve every binding.

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: a condition detectable early must be checked early -- starting with whole-base movement
decisions.rationale: The stale-base guard is asymmetric. scripts/factory_evidence.py --currency-only runs in the first seconds of validation and checks trust_root_drift(head): TRUST-ROOT files only. harness/merge_verify.py:149 checks whole-main movement -- `current_base != base` -- and runs only at merge pre-authorization, after the full ladder. A base moved by a commit that touches no trust-root file therefore passes every early check and refuses at the end, so the PR pays ~83 minutes to learn something knowable in one gh call at second zero. Observed 2026-09-09: PR #134 was re-headed onto c19546e, then #157 (one line of docs/atlas/register/decisions.json) merged. Nothing early would have caught it; the run was not started, and a second re-head was paid instead.
decisions.cost: one gh call at an existing rung
decisions.note: FIX: run the whole-base comparison at the same rung as --currency-only, not only at merge pre-authorization. merge_verify keeps its check -- it is the authority and must re-ask -- but it stops being the FIRST asker. THE CLASS, which matters more than this instance: a condition that is cheap and detectable early being checked late. This is the second recorded instance. The first was mutation injectability, which reported not_injected only in the full harness fifty minutes in until PR #139 moved it to the head of the static rung -- thirteen maintainer PRs had moved anchors in the meantime because nothing a maintainer met could see the drift. Both have the same shape: the authority that can answer cheaply is not asked until something expensive has already run. A third instance is likelier than not; look for it wherever a late gate reads state that was available at the start. DFE-017 reaches for this class from the other direction -- it asks that a floor move when what it measures moves; this asks that a check run when its input is first knowable. Neither subsumes the other and both are about a gate that exists but fires at the wrong time. SEPARATE FROM DFE-020: that is recovery (what a PR may do after a refusal), this is detection (when the refusal arrives).

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: a rung's observed measurement must survive a later rung's failure
decisions.rationale: Every observed floor value is written once, at the end, by scripts/factory_evidence.py. parse_harness dies unless the text carries `GATE_OK mode=full`, so a lap that fails at any rung discards the measurements of every rung that passed before it. Observed 2026-09-09, run 34379226169: E2E PASSED for the first time under this kernel -- provably, because the mutation rung runs after it and ran -- and `E2E_PASSED steps=N` is GONE. It was printed to evidence.log, which is deliberately excluded from artifact upload because that program holds credentials, and the refusal record's detail is capped at 2000 characters of tail. No bundle was written because mutations failed twenty minutes later, for an unrelated reason (an immunity text assertion pinning a signature DFE-014 had changed). The one number .factory/locks/floor.json has been waiting months for was observed and thrown away.
decisions.cost: a scrubbed per-rung measurements file; the ratcheting question is separate
decisions.note: DIFFERENT SHAPE from its neighbours, which is why it is its own entry. DFE-021 is a check that runs too late. DFE-017 is a floor that does not move when what it measures moves. This is a RESULT THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE AN UNRELATED LATER FAILURE -- the rung passed, the measurement existed, and nothing kept it. PROPOSED FIX: each rung appends its observed counts to a scrubbed, uploadable measurements file as it passes, rather than the bundle being assembled once at the end. Such a file is integers and rung names by construction, so it carries no secret and needs no exclusion. It must be OBSERVABILITY, like stage-timings.jsonl: the evidence bundle stays the sole authority and nothing reads the file to decide anything. Its purpose is that a failed lap still says what it proved. DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN, because it is a judgement about proof and not about plumbing: whether a measurement from a lap that later failed may SET a floor. The floor file's own rule says the value comes from a complete cycle, and parse_harness reads measurements only behind GATE_OK. Recording the number is unambiguously right; ratcheting from it is not, and this amendment does not claim it. Decide that separately or the fix quietly weakens the floors it was meant to serve.

decisions.title: AMENDMENT: a defanged detector reports protection it is not providing, and MUTATION_ANCHORS_OK cannot tell
decisions.rationale: THE POINT: an escape is visible; a defanged-but-caught defect is invisible. harness/mutation_anchors.py verifies each defect's `find` string occurs exactly once in the file it names. It does not verify the defect still tests what it was written to test. So a defect whose anchor was moved onto adjacent text can go on being CAUGHT -- by something incidental to the property it guards -- and the catalogue will report an invariant as protected while nothing checks that invariant. The failure mode is silence, and no number of laps surfaces it. That inverts what the catalogue is for: a mutation suite exists to prove a detector would notice, and this one can now assert a protection it is not providing. MUTATION_ANCHORS_OK reads as `the catalogue is intact` and means `every find string is present exactly once`. That is the constitution's honesty rule pointed inward -- an authority displaying OK for a property it never examined. THE GAP WAS KNOWN AND UNENFORCED: the program's own docstring names both correct branches (re-anchor onto the code that carries the property today, or say the property is gone and remove the defect deliberately) and checks neither. OBSERVED 2026-09-09. Nine defects were re-anchored on 746aac7 after DFE-014 moved the text they pinned. TWO were defanged. (1) worker-resume-also-dispatches: its `why` says the dispatch step would lose its inverse guard and run after a resume too. The anchor was moved onto the adjacent `id: dispatch` line and the replace renames the step id to `dispatch2`, leaving `if: inputs.resume_pr == '' && ...` intact. ESCAPED in run 34385357401 after 2072 s, 427 of 428 caught. (2) pack-verified-after-holdout: its `why` says verify_pack must precede the judge that relies on it. The original find spanned the pack call, the stage line and the whole _holdout_proof_summary block, and its replace MOVED THE PACK FETCH AFTER THE HOLDOUT. The re-anchor truncated find to two lines and produced a replace that changes one cursor label from attached_evidence to code_holdout. The pack call does not move. The mutation no longer tests ordering at all -- and it was CAUGHT, by something label-sensitive, so it is green and would have stayed green indefinitely. TODAY'S TWO VISIBLE FAILURES WERE THE LUCKY ONES. The immunity assertion and the escape both failed loudly and cost one lap each. The second defanged defect cost nothing, said nothing, and was found by reading.
decisions.cost: unknown; the decidable part is small, the rest may not be decidable at all
decisions.note: COMPLETE EXPOSURE, not a sample. A defect can only be defanged by someone moving its anchor, so the population at risk is every defect whose find/replace has ever changed after creation. A git walk of both catalogues across all 82 commits that touched them gives 37 defects: 22 in d90bac3e (PR #139, which re-pointed twenty-three anchors in one change so the mutation rung would stop reporting not_injected), 7 in 746aac7 (PR #155, audited -- 2 defanged), and 8 across six other commits. Under fifty, enumerable, and nobody has ever checked any of them for preserved meaning. THE REVIEW STEP THAT FOUND IT, which is the tractable part and is currently never asked: do not compare the mutation to prose. Compare WHAT THE REPLACE DOES against WHAT THE `why` CLAIMS THE DEFECT TESTS. For pack-verified-after-holdout the `why` names an ordering and the replace moves nothing -- visible at a glance, answerable by a human in seconds. It generalises: a `why` that names an ordering needs a replace that reorders; one that names a removed guard needs a replace that removes it; one that names a credential needs a replace that touches it. Make it a required question on any PR that changes a find or a replace. THE DULLER ALTERNATIVE, which answers the real question instead of approximating it: require a re-anchored defect to be RE-RUN before its PR merges. Expensive per change, exact. WHY NEITHER BECOMES A STATIC REFUSAL: the mechanisable form -- does the replace alter anything the `why` names -- is a heuristic over prose. It can warn. A gate that refuses on it would be asserting a judgement about meaning with the confidence of a measurement, which is the fake precision DFA-017 forbids, and it would be the same error this entry is about one level up. The general question, does this mutation still test what it was written to test, asks whether a program change defeats an unspecified set of detectors. That IS the mutation run. Do not specify a static check claiming to answer it. THE CHEAP INSTRUMENT IS CURRENTLY UNAVAILABLE, which is why today cost four laps. harness/factory_mutations/run.py refuses with `focused baseline is red` before mutating anything, because the 32 pre-existing genesis-ceremony failures make the local baseline red (BOOTSTRAP_REFUSED harness/genesis_validate.py does not match the validation_driver_sha256 the policy pins). The refusal is correct -- mutating against a red baseline proves nothing -- but the consequence is that the catalogue cannot be tested anywhere except inside a full lap. Those failures are not on the critical path and are not caused by any change here; they have nonetheless removed the only tool that could have made today cheaper. Worth its own entry if it persists.
